scenario: Fracture placed in a neighbouring bone + two normal statements + SPU
description: Built from msk-xr/findings_{gt,pred}/example_2 (constructed hand radiographs after a punch injury). The metacarpal neck fracture is matched although the pred places it in the fourth metacarpal (no gt fracture there; the bone is a location error downstream); the alignment and dislocation statements are two normal assessments of the joints; the foreign body the gt never mentions is SPU (no gt statement denies it).

user.indication: 24-year-old man with right hand pain and swelling after punching a wall.

pred_findings.text: Acute fracture of the right fourth metacarpal neck with approximately 35 degrees of volar angulation of the distal fragment.
Normal alignment at the carpometacarpal and metacarpophalangeal joints.
Radiopaque foreign body in the dorsal soft tissues over the right fifth metacarpophalangeal joint.

gt_findings.text: Acute fracture of the right fifth metacarpal neck with approximately 35 degrees of volar angulation of the distal fragment.

matches.reasoning: One metacarpal neck fracture, placed in the fourth vs fifth metacarpal.
Normal joint alignment and no dislocation are one assessment of the joints.
